conviction_note: The fundamental read is a mild EPS beat: the $0.11 consensus implies about a 22.5% Q3 gross margin, below Q2's 23.9% once the NRV reserve release is stripped out, and Q3 rode the hottest US summer on record. Against that, distributor glut commentary, Chemours' aftermarket destocking and Watsco's +2% in other HVAC products all point to subdued pricing, which the company already guided to. The name has fallen on its last four prints (-9.0, -19.0, -10.6, -22.4), so the reaction function vetoes most of the fundamental lean. p_up 53 on abs_move 12 gives +0.72, a little below the +0.80 sum of the findings. The two measurements agree in sign, and the gap is the reaction-history discount.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $0.11, from two agreeing sources: Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HDSN, which also confirms the Oct 28 amc date) and Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HDSN/earnings-forecasts, via search snippet). The revenue bar is disputed: $75.5M (an earlier Earnings Whispers figure), $78.3M (Benzinga) and $79.42M (the current Earnings Whispers page), so findings that depend on revenue are capped small. The company gave no Q3 revenue guide. Its only guide is FY2026 gross margin of 'low-to-mid-twenty percent', cut from mid-twenties on 2026-08-05 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000925528/000110465926091092/tm2622080d1_ex99-1.htm). Q3 2025 comparison: revenue $74.0M, GM 32.0%, EPS $0.27.
positioning_check: Short interest is 2,594,444 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 6.2% of 42.09M shares outstanding, with days to cover of 8.63, up from 5.94 on 09-30 as volume fell. Shares short have come down from 3.17M on 08-31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/hdsn/shortinterest). Moderate rather than crowded, but the high days to cover means a beat could squeeze. Hartree Partners, a 10% owner, bought 118,549 shares on 2026-09-24 at $5.10 and now holds 5,348,517 shares (about 12.7%) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/925528/000092189526002658/xslF345X06/form414670002_09282026.xml). It has filed Form 4 purchases continuously since July. Options: the chain is unusable (ATM spread 108% of mid), so there is no skew number. ATM IV is 75.8%, put/call OI 0.36 and total OI 1,705. Tape: spot $5.17, -4.44% over 5 days, +0.39% over 20 days, -44.5% from the 52-week high and +6.8% off the low.

findings.finding: Summer 2026 (June-August) was the warmest on record for the contiguous US per NOAA NCEI: 74.4F, 3.0F above average and 0.4F above the 1936/2021 records, with July the warmest month ever recorded. That is a volume tailwind for R-410A/R-22 service refrigerant demand in Hudson's Q3, its peak quarter. Management said on the Q2 call that warmer El Nino weather 'may also benefit our business'. Revenue consensus is $75.5-79.4M against $74.0M in Q3 2025, after volume grew 12% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beat in Q2 2026 ($78.3M vs about $75.8M consensus) and the stock still fell 9.0% on the EPS miss. Q3 2025 revenue grew 20% and beat, and the stock fell (-6.3% on the CEO exit, then -22.4% on a downgrade). Revenue beats have not been paid on this name.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (NCEI August 2026 national climate report; corroborated by https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2026/09/10/contiguous-us-records-warmest-summer-on-record)
findings.why_not_priced: The weather is public, and the rise in the Earnings Whispers revenue estimate from $75.5M to $79.4M may already reflect it. The EPS bar sits at $0.11, less than half of last year's $0.27. If the market had priced a strong heat-driven volume quarter, the stock would not sit 6.8% off its 52-week low after a 5-day -4.4% drift. Macro-to-company transmission is unconfirmed by the company beyond its Q2 remark.
findings.independence: This is a proxy. Watsco's Q3 (Oct 27) showed residential equipment +7% but other HVAC products (which include refrigerant) only +2% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000105016/000119312526432680/wso-ex99_1.htm), which tempers the read. It is filed separately as a negative.

findings.finding: The $0.11 Q3 EPS consensus implies roughly a 22.5% gross margin: revenue of about $79M, SG&A of about $11.5M, a 27% tax rate and 42.1M shares. Hudson's own Q2 gross margin was 26.4% reported, and 23.9% underlying once the $2.0M lower-of-cost-or-NRV reserve release is stripped out. The 10-Qs show the reserve at $9.96M at Dec-25, $7.05M at Mar-26 and $5.0M at Jun-26. $5.0M of reserve remains, and more can be released as Q3 sells reserved inventory if prices hold near the $6/lb that management called stabilizing. So the bar sits below the company's own run-rate, provided pricing did not fall further in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin/EPS is the line this stock trades on. Q2 2026 EPS of $0.12 missed $0.17-0.18 → -9.0%. Q1 2026 EPS missed and GM fell to 20% → -19.0%. Q4 2025 had an 8.0% GM with a $4.2M inventory/LCM charge → -10.6%. No recent EPS beat to measure the upside reaction; the Q3 2025 EPS beat ($0.27 vs $0.20) was swamped by a CEO exit and a downgrade.
findings.why_not_priced: The NRV reserve walk sits in 10-Q Note 3 and the cash-flow statement, not in the press release that wires and aggregators summarise. Analysts cut to $0.11 after a large Q2 miss, which may have overshot. If the market saw the bar as beatable, the stock would not have drifted -4.4% into the print near its 52-week low. Caveat: a renewed fall in HFC prices would turn the reserve into a charge, as in Q4 2025. The range covers that.
findings.independence: Q1 10-Q for the March reserve: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000925528/000110465926058632/hdsn-20260331x10q.htm. Same company documents, so not independent. The $6/lb stabilization comment comes from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/12/hudson-technologies-hdsn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

findings.finding: ACHR News (2026-08-12) reported a 'significant glut of virgin R-410A', with nearly 80% of HARDI distributors at or above target R-410A inventory before the season. That points to continued weak HFC pricing in Q3, against Q3 2025's elevated pricing (32% GM), so year-on-year pricing is likely down again (Q2 was -6%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pricing pressure drove the Q3 2024 print (-21% intraday on 'ongoing pricing pressure') and the 2026 GM misses (-19.0%, -9.0%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Hudson itself guided to 'continued subdued refrigerant market pricing ... through the close of 2026' and cut its FY margin guide, so this lands inside the guide. Kept small because the trade press says glut while management said stabilizing.
findings.independence: Chemours' Q3 TSS guide (separate finding) points the same way from a direct producer. Hudson's own 'trough in HFC prices' language (8-K, 2026-08-05) agrees.

findings.finding: Chemours guided Q3 2026 Thermal & Specialized Solutions sales down mid-teens to 20% sequentially on weaker Opteon blends aftermarket demand and residential AC aftermarket destocking, with higher rates and weak housing. That is a refrigerant producer's read of the same aftermarket channel Hudson sells into, given before Hudson's Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of HDSN reacting to Chemours guides. HDSN's own aftermarket pricing weakness drove the -19.0% and -9.0% prints in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since early August and mostly about A2L/HFO Opteon blends rather than HFC reclaim, so the transfer to Hudson is partial. Chemours does not report Q3 until Nov 2, after this window, so no fresh producer read exists. Small.
findings.independence: Proxy. It shares a theme with the ACHR glut finding but is a different source and a different product (HFO blends vs R-410A).

findings.finding: The channel that has reported since Hudson last spoke was mixed. Watsco Q3 2026 (2026-10-27): other HVAC products, which include refrigerant and supplies (29% of sales), +2% same-store, with residential equipment +7% and residential markets 'stabilizing'. Lennox Q3 2026 (2026-10-28, bmo): residential revenue +3% with segment margin -490bp on 'heightened competitive pressure'. A record summer produced only low-single-digit growth in the channel's refrigerant-inclusive line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of HDSN reacting to distributor prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Both are a day or two old and macro-level, so they are likely in the price already. Watsco does not break out refrigerant, so the transfer to Hudson is inference.
findings.independence: Lennox Q3 2026 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069202/000106920226000094/lii-20260930xexx991pressre.htm. It offsets the weather finding in part.

findings.finding: Hartree Partners, a 10% owner (now about 5.35M shares, roughly 12.7% of 42.1M outstanding), kept buying in the open market into late September: 118,549 shares on 2026-09-24 at a $5.10 average, with Form 4s on 08-14, 08-26, 09-04, 09-18, 09-23 and 09-28. The holder previously filed a 13D (2025) before switching to 13G. That gives a persistent strategic bid near the current $5.17 spot.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured. Hartree's buying through July-September did not stop the stock falling from about $6 to $5.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 4s by a commodity merchant on a microcap get little coverage. It offers a cushion against a negative print rather than a catalyst. If priced as a takeover option, the stock would not be 44% off its high.

findings.finding: Short interest is 2.59M shares (about 6.2% of shares outstanding) with days to cover rising to 8.63 at the 2026-10-15 settlement (from 5.94 on 09-30, 3.57 on 08-31) as volume thins. A beat would meet a short base that needs more than a week of average volume to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze has occurred on the last four prints, all of which fell.
findings.why_not_priced: Public FINRA data at a moderate level, so the shorts are not visibly crowded. It only matters conditional on a beat.
findings.independence: Curvedtrading also shows about 2.1M short in July with a low 0.7% borrow fee (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/hdsn/), so borrow is easy and the base is not crowded.

findings.finding: Mid-June tornado damage to an Illinois facility: management said restoration and business-interruption costs are expected to be covered by insurance and were excluded from Q2 results. Recognition of insurance recoveries or a business-interruption gain could fall in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history. A one-off below the gross margin line with no path to the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Amount and timing were not disclosed, and the Q2 call said 'major repairs are underway'. Sized at a fraction because it is a one-off.

findings.finding: Q2 SG&A of $12.4M (vs $9.3M) carried DLA bid-protest legal costs and more than $1M of H1 ERP optimisation costs. The DLA contract was re-awarded on 2026-08-04, and management said ERP costs 'will be lower in the second half' and that H2 SG&A increases would be smaller than H1's. Q3 SG&A should step down from Q2, against Q3 2025's $8.9M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SG&A growth was part of the Q1 and Q2 2026 EPS misses (-19.0%, -9.0%).
findings.why_not_priced: This is inside what management guided, so analysts should have modelled it. Kept small.
findings.independence: DLA re-award in the 10-Q subsequent events (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000925528/000110465926092682/hdsn-20260630x10q.htm).

outside_window.finding: EPA set 2027 HFC caps at about 60% of baseline (the statutory schedule, unchanged). The 2029 step-down to 30% of baseline is the real catalyst for reclaim pricing, and it lies years outside this window.
Chemours (Nov 2-3) and Solstice (Nov 4) Q3 2026 refrigerant results, the next direct producer reads on HFC/HFO pricing. Both are dated after the exit window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The mild positive lean (a beatable EPS bar and record heat) cuts against the name's habit of falling on prints (four straight down, median |move| 11.7%), so p_up stays near 50. The flat 20-day and -4.4% 5-day tape show no run-up to fade.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6: the revenue bar is disputed ($75.5M/$78.3M/$79.4M), so the weather finding, which depends on revenue, is capped smaller: 1.0 to 0.5, together with lesson 5 (macro-to-company proxy).
Lesson 1: this name has fallen on its last four prints including revenue beats, so the consensus-margin finding goes from 1.0 to 0.7 and p_up from 54 to 53.

Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the ACHR glut finding goes from -0.5 to -0.3 and the Chemours destocking finding from -0.5 to -0.4, because Hudson already guided to 'continued subdued pricing'. The SG&A step-down goes from 0.2 to 0.1 because management guided it.
Lesson 2: tornado insurance one-off from 0.2 to 0.1.
Lesson 5: short-interest positioning from 0.2 to 0.1, because positioning alone is weak evidence on a microcap.
Left standing: Hartree's buying at 0.3, the Watsco/Lennox proxy at -0.3, and abs_move_pct at 12 (lesson 8 argues against shrinking it).
